title: TabICLv2: A Better, Faster, Scalable, and Open Tabular Foundation Model
claim: Our model reaches the best accuracy at low compute cost, dominating the accuracy-versus-runtime Pareto front over all competing methods.
layout: 1 scatter plot with side legend; Pareto front dashed line, 'Optimal' arrow
description: A single scatter plot with train time per 1K samples on a log x-axis (10^-1 to 10^4 seconds) and improvability (lower is better) on the y-axis (about 5% to 25%). Many colored markers represent methods. Circles are default settings, squares are tuned, and crosses are tuned plus ensemble. Methods are color-coded in a long legend on the right. A dashed black Pareto-front staircase runs from the top left down to the bottom. A green arrow labeled 'Optimal' points to the lower-left corner. The one black circle, TabICLv2-D, sits alone near the bottom left in a boxed label, with a lower error than every other method. Tuned and ensembled baselines cluster at the right with slower runtimes and higher error. The eye goes first to the isolated black point.
caption: Improvability vs.\ train time on TabArena [ref]. Improvability (lower is better) measures the relative error gap to the best method, averaged across datasets. Train time is training + inference in 8-fold cross-validation. For foundation models, it is dominated by forward passes that perform in-context learning. Default uses default hyperparameters; Tuned selects the best of 200 random hyperparameter configurations on validation; Tuned + Ens. applies post-hoc weighted ensemble of all configurations. The runtime of \name is measured on an H100 GPU, while others are from TabArena. Results for inapplicable model-dataset pairs are imputed with default RandomForest.
abstract: Tabular foundation models, such as TabPFNv2 and TabICL, have recently dethroned gradient-boosted trees at the top of predictive benchmarks, demonstrating the value of in-context learning for tabular data. We introduce TabICLv2, a new state-of-the-art foundation model for regression and classification built on three pillars: (1) a novel synthetic data generation engine designed for high pretraining diversity; (2) various architectural innovations, including a new scalable softmax in attention improving generalization to larger datasets without prohibitive long-sequence pretraining; and (3) optimized pretraining protocols, notably replacing AdamW with the Muon optimizer. On the TabArena and TALENT benchmarks, TabICLv2 without any tuning surpasses the performance of the current state of the art, RealTabPFN-2.5 (hyperparameter-tuned, ensembled, and fine-tuned on real data). With only moderate pretraining compute, TabICLv2 generalizes effectively to million-scale datasets under 50 GB GPU memory while being markedly faster than RealTabPFN-2.5. We provide extensive ablation studies to quantify these contributions and foster open research by releasing code for inference, pretraining, and synthetic data generation at https://github.com/soda-inria/tabicl.
